# Dependency ledger

Date: 30 August 2026

Status: exact staging metadata only. This packet is not included by the live
manuscript and has not been submitted to production Rethlas.

## Wrapper identifiers

The candidate results have no `\label` commands in the frozen statement or
proof. The compile wrapper records only these editorial identifiers:

- Candidate A: `prop:p061-frobenius-rpl-descent`
- Candidate B: `thm:p061-simplicial-toric-ph-rpl`

No conventional theorem name, novelty claim, or priority claim is attached.

## Dependency graph

```text
D3 + D4 ----------------------------> Candidate A
Candidate A + D1 + D2 + D3 + D5
            + D6 + D7 + internal
            lattice/Frobenius proof -> Candidate B
```

All lattice, semigroup-ring, characteristic decomposition, radiciality,
affinoid `q`-power, Reynolds-projector, and non-full-dimensional arguments are
proved in the candidate proof itself.

## D1 — production-verified quasi-smooth P06.1 input

Exact live label: `thm:p061-quasismooth-ph-rpl`.

Statement used: if $K$ is complete and nontrivially valued and $X$ is a
good strict quasi-smooth $K$-analytic space, then every classically
pluriharmonic real function on $X$ is real-PL and GJR harmonic. There is no
global quasicompactness, separatedness, or boundarylessness hypothesis.

Frozen packet:

## D2 — production-verified finite constant-group descent

Exact live label: `prop:p061-finite-group-rpl-descent-candidate`.

Statement used: let a finite constant group $G$ act analytically on a
separated strict affinoid $Y$, with analytic categorical quotient
$q:Y\to X=Y/G$. If a continuous real function $g$ on $X$ has real-PL
pullback, then $g$ is real-PL. No flatness, étaleness, freeness,
reducedness, normality, or restriction on the group order in the ground or
residue field is assumed.

Frozen packet:

- `manuscript/editorial/rethlas_packets_20260830/`
  `p061_finite_quotient_gdescent_audit_20260830/`
- statement: `p061_gdescent_candidate_statement_20260830.tex`
- proof: `p061_gdescent_candidate_proof_20260830.tex`
- statement SHA-256:
  `e1daa4b3e3efd64fcc8f0ce05b9c1d5d6cb69b28686b939b48535fc56b0ccc07`
- proof SHA-256:
  `a6c24d1686c726dc72aebe55a1e83eb8d4fe1ed4025d4a8d7166da59123ce30e`
- production run: `20260829T235341Z_e1daa4b3e3ef`
- verdict: `correct`, zero critical errors, zero gaps.

The candidate proof separately verifies that the split prime-to-$p$
restriction over each target affinoid is the analytic categorical quotient
required by D2.

## D3 — published real-PL and harmonic definitions

Walter Gubler, Philipp Jell, and Joseph Rabinoff, *Forms on Berkovich spaces
based on harmonic tropicalizations*, BSMF 154 (2026), 135–238,
DOI `10.24033/bsmf.2919`.

Exact portions used:

- Definition 5.1: a real-PL function is G-locally a finite real linear
  combination of logarithms of analytic units.
- §5.2(3): restriction to a strictly analytic domain preserves real-PL.
- §5.2(4): real-PL functions form a sheaf for the G-topology and hence the
  analytic topology.
- Definition 7.2: an R-PL function is harmonic exactly when it and its
  negative are semipositive at every point.

Official primary PDF:
`https://smf.emath.fr/system/files/filepdf/GUBLER_JELL_RABINOFF.pdf`.

## D4 — rational refinement and finite analytic base change

Two foundational inputs are used.

1. Gerritzen–Grauert: every affinoid domain of a strict affinoid space has a
   finite cover by rational domains. Exact primary locator: Michael Temkin,
   *A new proof of the Gerritzen–Grauert theorem*, Theorem 1.1 and the
   explicit consequence in the introduction; the paper identifies the
   classical locator as BGR 7.3.5/1.
   `https://math.huji.ac.il/~temkin/papers/Gerritzen_Grauert.pdf`.
2. Affinoid fibre products and finite morphisms: for affinoids, the fibre
   product algebra is the completed tensor product; a finite morphism pulls
   back every target affinoid to an affinoid with finite algebra. Exact
   locators: Michael Temkin, *Introduction to Berkovich analytic spaces*,
   Fact 4.1.16 and Definition 4.2.5.
   `https://berkovich-2010.imj-prg.fr/lecture-notes/Temkin-lecture-notes.pdf`.

The only completion issue needed here is also proved directly: a tensor
product which is finite over an affinoid algebra is already complete because
finite submodules of finite affinoid modules are closed.

## D5 — published classical pluriharmonic functoriality

Walter Gubler and Joseph Rabinoff, *Classically psh and pluriharmonic
functions on Berkovich spaces*, arXiv:2506.13548v2.

Exact portions used:

- Proposition 7.2(6): a real function is classically pluriharmonic if and
  only if its scalar pullback along an analytic extension field is.
- Proposition 7.2(7), forward direction: arbitrary analytic pullback
  preserves classical pluriharmonicity.

Local primary PDF:

- `manuscript/editorial/rethlas_packets_20260830/`
  `p031_perfected_unibranch_curve_envelope_20260830/sources/`
  `Gubler_Rabinoff_2506.13548v2.pdf`
- SHA-256:
  `83ca9a19394f44bb2e4e1aa316de95938f311acd53a00fe250fa0f605184b726`

Official URL: `https://arxiv.org/pdf/2506.13548v2`.

## D6 — published scalar descent for real-PL functions

Gubler–Jell–Rabinoff, Corollary 5.12: if $X$ is good and strict,
$K'/K$ is the completion of an algebraic extension, and the coefficient
group is divisible, then a real function on $X$ is PL with those
coefficients if and only if its scalar pullback to $X_{K'}$ is. Candidate
B applies this with the divisible group $\mathbf R$ and a finite, hence
complete, extension $L/K$.

Primary source and URL are those in D3.

## D7 — published classical psh/semipositivity comparison

Gubler–Rabinoff, Theorem 4.3: over a nontrivially valued field, an R-PL
function on a good strict analytic space is semipositive if and only if it is
classically psh. Candidate B applies this to both $h$ and $-h$, then uses
D3, Definition 7.2.

Primary source, local PDF, hash, and URL are those in D5.

## Excluded dependencies

The proof does **not** use GJR Proposition 5.11 (finite-flat PL descent), a
trace or norm, perfectness of $K$, a constant presentation of the
$p$-primary diagonalizable factor, ordinary analytic étale descent,
log-étale comparison, or any non-simplicial toric uniformization.

% Exact quarantined statement for P06.1.
% This file is not included by the live manuscript.
% It makes no novelty or priority claim.

\begin{lemma}
\label{lem:p061-rigid-etale-rpl-descent}
Let \(K\) be a complete non-Archimedean field with nontrivial absolute
value.  Let \(U\) and \(V\) be strict \(K\)-affinoid rigid spaces, and let
\[
                         q:V\longrightarrow U
\]
be a covering for the rigid \(\acute{e}\)tale topology.  Write
\(U^{\mathrm B}\) and \(V^{\mathrm B}\) for the associated Berkovich
spaces.  If \(g:U^{\mathrm B}\to\mathbf R\) is continuous and
\(g\circ q^{\mathrm B}\) is \(\mathbf R\)-PL, then \(g\) is
\(\mathbf R\)-PL.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}
\label{thm:p061-quasismooth-ph-rpl}
Let \(K\) be a complete non-Archimedean field with nontrivial absolute
value, and let \(X\) be a good, strict, quasi-smooth \(K\)-analytic space.
Then every classically pluriharmonic function
\[
                             h:X\longrightarrow\mathbf R
\]
is \(\mathbf R\)-PL.  Equivalently, \(h\) is G-locally a finite real
linear combination of functions \(\log|f|\), with \(f\) an analytic unit.
Moreover, \(h\) is harmonic in the sense of
Gubler--Jell--Rabinoff.  No global quasicompactness, separatedness, or
boundarylessness hypothesis is required.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proposition}
\label{prop:p061-integral-pl-counterexample}
The conclusion of \Cref{thm:p061-quasismooth-ph-rpl} cannot be strengthened
from \(\mathbf R\)-PL to integral PL, or even to \(\mathbf Q\)-PL.  More
precisely, choose
\(\pi\in K\) with \(0<|\pi|<1\), put
\[
 X=\mathcal M\bigl(K\langle T,S\rangle/(TS-\pi)\bigr),
 \qquad h=\sqrt2\log|T|,
\]
and regard \(X\) as the closed annulus \(|\pi|\leq |T|\leq1\).  Then \(X\)
is good, compact, strict, and quasi-smooth, and it has a strictly semistable
formal \(K^\circ\)-model.  The function \(h\) is classically
pluriharmonic and \(\mathbf R\)-PL, but it is not \(\mathbf Q\)-PL and hence
is not integral PL.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proposition}\label{prop:p061-finite-group-rpl-descent-candidate}
Let $K$ be a complete non-Archimedean field with nontrivial absolute value.
Let $Y=\mathcal M(A)$ be a separated strict $K$-affinoid space, let a finite
constant group $G$ act analytically on $Y$, and let
\[
                         q:Y\longrightarrow X:=Y/G
\]
be the analytic categorical quotient.  Let $g:X\to\mathbf R$ be continuous.
If $q^*g$ is $\mathbf R$-PL, then $g$ is $\mathbf R$-PL.
No flatness, \'etaleness, freeness, reducedness, normality, or restriction on
$|G|$ in $K$ or in the residue field is required.
\end{proposition}

% Exact live statement prepared from the production-verified staged statement.
% No conventional theorem name, novelty claim, or priority claim is attached.

\begin{proposition}
\label{prop:p061-frobenius-rpl-descent}
Let \(K\) be a complete non-Archimedean field with nontrivial absolute
value and characteristic \(p>0\).  Let
\[
                         f:Y\longrightarrow X
\]
be a finite, surjective, radicial morphism of good strict \(K\)-analytic
spaces, and assume that \(X\) is reduced.  Suppose that there is a power
\(q=p^e\), with \(e\geq 0\), such that the following holds for every strict
affinoid domain \(U=\mathcal M(C)\) in \(X\).  If
\(f^{-1}(U)=\mathcal M(D)\), then the induced homomorphism
\(C\hookrightarrow D\) is injective and
\[
                              D^q\subseteq C.
\]
Here the inclusion means that \(d^q\) belongs to the image of \(C\) for
every \(d\in D\).

Let \(g:X\to\mathbf R\) be continuous.  If \(f^*g\) is
\(\mathbf R\)-PL, then \(g\) is \(\mathbf R\)-PL.
\end{proposition}

## Internally proved claims

No external source is needed for the following steps because the exact proof
contains the complete argument:

- saturation and splitting of $N\cap\operatorname{span}_{\mathbf R}\sigma$;
- the non-full-dimensional decomposition
  $X_{\sigma,N'}\simeq\mathbf A^r\times\mathbf G_m^{n-r}$;
- finiteness and diagonalizable invariant algebra of the lattice cover;
- the canonical $p$-primary/prime-to-$p$ lattice factorization;
- existence of the finite roots-of-unity splitting field;

% Exact quarantined source-aware proof for P06.1.
% This file is not included by the live manuscript.
% It makes no novelty or priority claim.

\begin{proof}[Proof of \Cref{lem:p061-rigid-etale-rpl-descent}]
Work on the rigid \(\acute{e}\)tale site \(U_{\mathrm{\acute et}}\) of
de Jong--van der Put.  For an object \(W\to U\), define \(\mathscr P(W)\)
to be the compatible families of \(\mathbf R\)-PL functions on all strict
affinoid G-domains of \(W\).  Thus it is the space of global sections of
the affinoid-local G-sheaf
\[
 A\longmapsto\operatorname{PL}_{\mathbf R}(A^{\mathrm B}).
\]
When \(W\) is affinoid, this is
\(\operatorname{PL}_{\mathbf R}(W^{\mathrm B})\).  This definition covers
all, including globally nongood, objects of the rigid
\(\acute{e}\)tale site.  Pullback makes \(\mathscr P\) a presheaf: on good
strict Berkovich spaces this is
\cite[Lemma~5.4(1)]{GJR26}, and the general rigid object follows by the
affinoid-local definition.

We verify the two conditions of
\cite[Proposition~3.2.2]{dJvdP96}.  First, the restriction of
\(\mathscr P\) to every rigid G-site is a sheaf by construction and
\cite[\S5.2(4)]{GJR26}.  The special rigid G-topology used by
de Jong--van der Put has the same category of sheaves as the usual strong
rigid G-topology by \cite[\S2.1]{dJvdP96}, so there is no change of sheaf
category in this step.

For the second condition, let \(f:W'\to W\) be a surjective finite
\(\acute{e}\)tale morphism of strict affinoid rigid spaces.  We prove
exactness of
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p061-finite-etale-equalizer}
  0\longrightarrow\mathscr P(W)\longrightarrow\mathscr P(W')
  \mathrel{\substack{\longrightarrow\\[-0.6ex]\longrightarrow}}
  \mathscr P(W'\times_W W').
\end{equation}
For clarity, \(f^{\mathrm B}\) is surjective: finite
\(\acute{e}\)taleness and surjectivity make the affinoid algebra map finite
faithfully flat, so its base change to \(\mathscr H(x)\) is a nonzero finite
algebra for every \(x\in W^{\mathrm B}\), and any maximal-ideal quotient
supplies a point above \(x\).  Injectivity in
\eqref{eq:p061-finite-etale-equalizer} follows.  Now take
\(s'\in\mathscr P(W')\) whose two pullbacks to \(W'\times_WW'\) agree.
We first show that \(s'\) is constant on every Berkovich fibre.  Let
\(y_1,y_2\in (W')^{\mathrm B}\) have common image
\(x\in W^{\mathrm B}\).  Since \(f\) is finite, each
\(\mathscr H(y_i)\) is a finite separable extension of \(\mathscr H(x)\).
Choose a common finite, hence complete, valued extension \(\Omega\) of
\(\mathscr H(x)\) and \(\mathscr H(x)\)-embeddings
\(\iota_i:\mathscr H(y_i)\hookrightarrow\Omega\).  The embeddings are
isometric because the absolute value has a unique extension to a finite
extension of a complete non-Archimedean field.  The bounded homomorphism
\[
 \mathscr H(y_1)\widehat\otimes_{\mathscr H(x)}\mathscr H(y_2)
 \longrightarrow\Omega,\qquad
 a\otimes b\longmapsto\iota_1(a)\iota_2(b),
\]
followed by the absolute value of \(\Omega\), is a bounded multiplicative
seminorm.  Its restriction to each factor is exactly the prescribed absolute
value defining \(y_i\), by the isometry just noted.  It therefore gives a
point \(z\) of
\((W'\times_WW')^{\mathrm B}\) whose two projections are \(y_1\) and
\(y_2\).  Equality of the two pullbacks at \(z\) gives
\(s'(y_1)=s'(y_2)\).

There is therefore a unique function \(s:W^{\mathrm B}\to\mathbf R\)
such that \(s'=s\circ f^{\mathrm B}\).  Both Berkovich affinoid spaces are
compact Hausdorff.  Thus the continuous surjection \(f^{\mathrm B}\) is
closed and is a quotient map.  Since \(s'\) is continuous, the defining
property of the quotient topology shows that \(s\) is continuous.  A
finite \(\acute{e}\)tale morphism is finite, flat, and surjective, so
\cite[Proposition~5.11]{GJR26}, applied with the divisible coefficient
group \(\mathbf R\), shows from
\(s'=f^*s\in\operatorname{PL}_{\mathbf R}(W')\) that
\(s\in\operatorname{PL}_{\mathbf R}(W)\).  This proves the equalizer
condition \eqref{eq:p061-finite-etale-equalizer}.

The criterion \cite[Proposition~3.2.2]{dJvdP96} now says that
\(\mathscr P\) is a sheaf for the rigid \(\acute{e}\)tale topology.  The
section \(g\circ q^{\mathrm B}\) belongs to \(\mathscr P(V)\), and its two
pullbacks to \(V\times_UV\) agree because it is pulled back from the
function \(g\).  Sheaf descent supplies a section \(s\in\mathscr P(U)\)
with \(s\circ q^{\mathrm B}=g\circ q^{\mathrm B}\).  The covering map is
surjective, so \(s=g\).  Hence \(g\) is \(\mathbf R\)-PL.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[Proof of \Cref{thm:p061-quasismooth-ph-rpl}]
Fix \(x\in X\).  Goodness and strictness give a strict affinoid
neighbourhood \(U\) of \(x\).  Quasi-smoothness is preserved on analytic
domains.  Under the rigid--Berkovich equivalence recalled in
\cite[\S3.4]{Temkin17}, let \(\mathcal U\) be the rigid space associated to
\(U\); it is smooth, quasicompact, and quasiseparated, and
\(\mathcal U^{\mathrm B}=U\).

Apply \cite[Corollary~3.3.2]{Temkin17}.  There are a finite extension
\(L/K\) and a covering in the rigid \(\acute{e}\)tale topology
\[
                 q:\mathcal V\longrightarrow\mathcal U_L
\]
such that \(\mathcal V\) is affinoid and possesses a strictly semistable
affine formal \(L^\circ\)-model.  This is the precise version needed below.
In particular, we do not replace it by the wording of
\cite[Theorem~3.4.1]{Temkin17}, and we do not assert that \(q\) itself is
finite or flat.

Let \(h_U=h|_U\).  The scalar extension \((h_U)_L\) is classically
pluriharmonic on \(\mathcal U_L^{\mathrm B}\) by
\cite[Proposition~7.2(6)]{GR25Classical}, and hence is continuous by the
opening assertion of that proposition.  Its pullback
\((q^{\mathrm B})^*(h_U)_L\) is classically pluriharmonic by the
arbitrary-morphism
direction of \cite[Proposition~7.2(7)]{GR25Classical}; relative boundary of
the associated quasi-\(\acute{e}\)tale Berkovich morphism causes no problem
for this functorial statement.

The space \(\mathcal V^{\mathrm B}\) is good, quasicompact, and strict and
has the strictly semistable formal model just supplied.  Therefore
\cite[Proposition~7.8]{GR25Classical} gives
\[
                   (q^{\mathrm B})^*(h_U)_L\in
                   \operatorname{PL}_{\mathbf R}(\mathcal V^{\mathrm B}).
\]
The complete \(\acute{e}\)tale descent in
\Cref{lem:p061-rigid-etale-rpl-descent} now gives
\((h_U)_L\in
\operatorname{PL}_{\mathbf R}(\mathcal U_L^{\mathrm B})\).  Since \(L/K\)
is finite, it is already complete and is the completion of an algebraic
extension.  Ground-field descent
\cite[Corollary~5.12]{GJR26}, again with coefficient group \(\mathbf R\),
gives
\(h_U\in\operatorname{PL}_{\mathbf R}(\mathcal U^{\mathrm B})
=\operatorname{PL}_{\mathbf R}(U)\).

Every point \(x\in X\) has such a neighbourhood \(U\), and
\(\mathbf R\)-PL functions form a G-sheaf by
\cite[\S5.2(4)]{GJR26}.  Hence
\(h\in\operatorname{PL}_{\mathbf R}(X)\).

Finally, both \(h\) and \(-h\) are classically psh by definition.  For an
\(\mathbf R\)-PL function on a good strict space,
\cite[Theorem~4.3]{GR25Classical} identifies classical psh with
semipositivity.  Thus both signs of \(h\) are semipositive, which is exactly
harmonicity in \cite[Definition~7.2]{GJR26}.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[Proof of \Cref{prop:p061-integral-pl-counterexample}]
The displayed annulus is the generic fibre of
\[
 \operatorname{Spf}
 \bigl(K^\circ\langle T,S\rangle/(TS-\pi)\bigr),
\]
a strictly semistable affine formal \(K^\circ\)-scheme.  In particular,
\(X\) has all of the regularity properties asserted in the proposition.
The function \(T\) is an analytic unit on \(X\).  Hence \(\log|T|\) is
classically pluriharmonic by \cite[Proposition~7.2(2)]{GR25Classical}, and
the real-vector-space property
\cite[Proposition~7.2(3)]{GR25Classical} makes
\(h=\sqrt2\log|T|\) classically pluriharmonic.  It is visibly
\(\mathbf R\)-PL from \cite[Definition~5.1]{GJR26}.

On the standard skeleton of \(X\), use the coordinate
\[
                   t=-\log|T|\in[0,-\log|\pi|].
\]
The restriction of \(h\) is the affine function \(-\sqrt2\,t\).  Suppose
that \(h\) were \(\mathbf Q\)-PL.  By
\cite[Definition~5.1]{GJR26}, there is an admissible G-cover on whose
members \(h\) is a finite \(\mathbf Q\)-linear combination of logarithms of
analytic units.  Refine by strict affinoid domains.  Since \(X\) is
affinoid, quasicompactness for the G-topology gives a finite subcover
\(X_1,\ldots,X_N\).  Let \(S\) denote the compact skeleton.  Each
\(F_i=X_i\cap S\) is closed in \(S\), because \(X_i\) is compact and \(S\)
is Hausdorff, and the \(F_i\) cover the nondegenerate interval \(S\).
The Baire theorem therefore gives an index \(i\) for which \(F_i\) contains
a nondegenerate relatively open skeletal interval \(J\).

On \(X_i\), write
\[
                         h=\sum_{j=1}^m q_j\log|f_j|,
             \qquad q_j\in\mathbf Q,\quad f_j\in\mathscr O(X_i)^\times.
\]
The integral-slope theorem for analytic units on a quasi-smooth analytic
curve says that the restriction of every \(\log|f_j|\) to the geodesic
skeletal interval \(J\subset X_i\) is locally piecewise affine with integral
slopes; this is the local content of
\cite[Proposition~2.2.24(i)]{Thu05}, after local semistable reduction.  Since
there are only finitely many \(f_j\), there is a nondegenerate subinterval
\(I\subset J\) on which all these restrictions are affine with integral
slopes.  Consequently the slope of \(h\) on \(I\) is rational.  Its actual
constant slope is \(-\sqrt2\), a
contradiction.  Thus \(h\) is not \(\mathbf Q\)-PL and, a fortiori, is not
integral PL.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}
Put $u=q^*g$.  Fix $x\in X$, choose $y\in q^{-1}(x)$, and set
$H:=G_y$.  Since $Y$ is Hausdorff, there is an ordinary open neighbourhood
$C$ of $y$ which is $H$-stable and whose translates indexed by $G/H$ are
pairwise disjoint.  The orbit topology and invariant structure sheaf for the
finite analytic quotient identify
\begin{equation}\label{eq:p061-clean-local-quotient-candidate}
                         C/H\simeq q(C),
\end{equation}
where $q(C)$ is an ordinary open neighbourhood of $x$ in $X$.

By Gubler--Jell--Rabinoff Proposition~5.8, after shrinking around $y$ in the
ordinary topology, there are $a_1,\ldots,a_m\in\mathbf R$ and integral PL
functions $h_1,\ldots,h_m$ such that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:p061-local-rpl-decomposition-candidate}
                              u=\sum_{i=1}^m a_i h_i.
\end{equation}
By adjoining the zero integral PL function with coefficient zero if
necessary, we may assume $m\geq1$.
Intersect this ordinary open with $C$ and with all its $H$-translates.  We may
therefore assume it is $H$-stable and contained in $C$.  Choose a strict
affinoid neighbourhood $N_0$ of $y$ in it and put
\[
                          N:=\bigcap_{\gamma\in H}\gamma N_0.
\]
Separatedness makes $N$ a strict affinoid domain.  Since every factor is an
ordinary neighbourhood of the $H$-fixed point $y$, $N$ is an $H$-stable
strict affinoid neighbourhood of $y$.  Write $N^\circ$ for its interior
relative to $C$.

We next record the formal-model construction, including the descent step
because the quotient $N\to N/H$ need not be flat.  Restrict the $h_i$ to
$N$.  By Gubler--Jell--Rabinoff~5.6 and Raynaud cofilteredness, they are model
functions on a common formal model.  This common model may be chosen
$H$-equivariant as follows.  Start with an $H$-stable affine formal model
$\mathfrak N_0$ of $N$.  For a model
$(\mathfrak N_i,\mathfrak L_i)$ inducing $h_i$, Raynaud cofilteredness gives
an admissible formal blowup $\mathfrak P_i\to\mathfrak N_0$ and a morphism
$\mathfrak P_i\to\mathfrak N_i$ inducing the identity on the generic fibre.
Take the schematic closure of the common diagonal generic fibre in the
fibre product
\[
       \prod_{\substack{\mathfrak N_0;\ 1\leq i\leq m,\ \gamma\in H}}
             \gamma^*\mathfrak P_i.
\]
After removing $K^\circ$-torsion, the resulting admissible formal model
$\mathfrak N$ is $H$-equivariant, and projection to the identity factors
pulls the line bundles back to line bundles, still denoted
$\mathfrak L_i\in M(\mathfrak N)$, satisfying
$h_i=h_{\mathfrak L_i}$.  Every $\mathfrak P_i\to\mathfrak N_0$ is
projective.  Thus $\mathfrak N$ is closed in a projective formal scheme over
the affine $\mathfrak N_0$, and its special fibre is quasi-projective.  Hence
Zavyalov Remark~3.3.3 and Theorem~3.3.4 construct the admissible formal
quotient $\pi:\mathfrak N\to\mathfrak X:=\mathfrak N/H$, and Zavyalov
Theorem~4.4.1 identifies the adic generic fibre of $\mathfrak X$ with the
adic quotient of $N$.  Passing to the associated strict Berkovich space, or
equivalently using the invariant affinoid algebra, identifies it with the
Berkovich quotient $N/H$.

For each $i$, define the tensor-induced line bundle
\[
        \mathfrak T_i:=\bigotimes_{\gamma\in H}\gamma^*\mathfrak L_i.
\]
It has a canonical $H$-linearization by reindexing the factors.  We claim
that it descends to a line bundle $\overline{\mathfrak L}_i$ on
$\mathfrak X$.  Indeed, fix a point of $\mathfrak X$.  Its inverse image is
one finite $H$-orbit.  On an affine neighbourhood of that orbit, semilocal
triviality of a rank-one projective module gives an open neighbourhood $V$
of the entire orbit and one frame $s$ of $\mathfrak L_i$ on $V$.  Replacing
$V$ by the intersection of its $H$-translates makes it $H$-stable while
preserving the frame.  Then
\[
                         \bigotimes_{\gamma\in H}\gamma^*s
\]
is an invariant frame of $\mathfrak T_i$.  Its image is an open subset of
$\mathfrak X$, and ratios of any two such invariant frames are invariant
units.  Since the quotient structure sheaf is the invariant structure sheaf,
those ratios descend to units and glue trivial line bundles on
$\mathfrak X$.  This proves the claim.  Tensoring the given generic
trivializations of the $\gamma^*\mathfrak L_i$ gives an invariant analytic
frame of $\mathfrak T_{i,\eta}$.  Its ratios with the invariant formal frames
just constructed are invariant analytic units, and therefore descend and
glue to a trivialization of $\overline{\mathfrak L}_{i,\eta}$.  Thus
$\overline{\mathfrak L}_i$ is indeed a model of the analytically trivial line
bundle, with trivialization pulling back to the tensor-product
trivialization.  Notice that this argument neither uses exactness of invariants nor
divides by $|H|$ in $K^\circ$.

Let $\overline h_i:=h_{\overline{\mathfrak L}_i}$ on $N/H$.  Compatibility
of model functions with pullback gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:p061-tensor-induction-pullback-candidate}
                  q_N^*\overline h_i
                     =\sum_{\gamma\in H}\gamma^*h_i.
\end{equation}
Consequently the $\mathbf R$-PL function
\[
                       v:=\frac1{|H|}\sum_{i=1}^m a_i\overline h_i
\]
on $N/H$ satisfies, by
\eqref{eq:p061-local-rpl-decomposition-candidate} and the $H$-invariance of
$u$,
\[
 q_N^*v
 =\frac1{|H|}\sum_{\gamma\in H}\gamma^*u
 =u|_N.
\]
The quotient $N^\circ/H$ is an ordinary open subset of both $N/H$ and
$C/H$.  Under \eqref{eq:p061-clean-local-quotient-candidate}, it is an
ordinary open neighbourhood of $x$.  Surjectivity of $q_N$ shows that $v$
restricts there to $g$.  Thus $g$ is $\mathbf R$-PL on an ordinary open
neighbourhood of every $x\in X$, and hence is $\mathbf R$-PL on $X$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}
The assertion is local for the \(G\)-topology on \(X\).  Fix a strict
affinoid domain \(U=\mathcal M(C)\) in \(X\), and put
\[
                V=f^{-1}(U)=\mathcal M(D),\qquad u=f^*g|_V.
\]
The space \(V\) is strict affinoid because \(f\) is finite.

We first record the point-set consequence of the hypotheses.  The map
\(V\to U\) is bijective.  Indeed, finiteness and surjectivity give at least
one lift of every support prime, while radiciality gives a unique lift and a
purely inseparable extension of residue fields.  An absolute value on a
field has a unique extension to a purely inseparable field extension: if
\(a^{p^r}\) lies in the smaller field, then its value must be
\[
                       |a|=|a^{p^r}|^{1/p^r}.
\]
Thus every Berkovich point has exactly one lift.  The resulting continuous
bijection \(V\to U\) is a homeomorphism because \(V\) is compact and \(U\)
is Hausdorff.

By \cite[Definition~5.1 and \S5.2(3),(4)]{GJR26}, \(u\) has a
\(G\)-cover by strict affinoid domains on which it is a finite real linear
combination of logarithms of analytic units.  Quasicompactness of the
strict affinoid \(V\) gives a finite subcover.  By the
Gerritzen--Grauert theorem \cite[Theorem~1.1]{Temkin2005GG}, each member
of this finite cover has a finite cover by rational domains of \(V\).  We
therefore obtain a finite rational \(G\)-cover \(\{W_\alpha\}_\alpha\) of
\(V\) such that
\begin{equation}
 \label{eq:p061-frobenius-upstairs-rpl}
       u|_{W_\alpha}
       =\sum_{j=1}^{m_\alpha}\lambda_{\alpha j}
                      \log|t_{\alpha j}|,
 \qquad
       \lambda_{\alpha j}\in\mathbf R,\quad
       t_{\alpha j}\in\mathcal O(W_\alpha)^\times .
\end{equation}

Fix one \(W=W_\alpha\).  Choose a rational presentation
\[
 W=\bigl\{y\in V:\ |b_i(y)|\leq |b_0(y)|,
                  \ 1\leq i\leq s\bigr\},
\]
where \(b_0,\ldots,b_s\in D\) generate the unit ideal.  Put
\(a_i=b_i^q\in C\).  Choose \(d_0,\ldots,d_s\in D\) with
\(1=\sum_i d_i b_i\).  Since \(q\) is a power of \(p\), Frobenius gives
\[
             1=\left(\sum_i d_i b_i\right)^q
              =\sum_i d_i^q a_i.
\]
Every \(d_i^q\) belongs to \(C\), and \(C\hookrightarrow D\) is injective,
so this is an identity in \(C\).  In particular,
\(a_0,\ldots,a_s\) generate the unit ideal.  Hence
\[
 U_W=\bigl\{x\in U:\ |a_i(x)|\leq |a_0(x)|,
                  \ 1\leq i\leq s\bigr\}
\]
is a rational domain in \(U\).

For the unique \(y\in V\) above \(x\in U\), one has
\(|a_i(x)|=|b_i(y)|^q\).  Consequently
\(f^{-1}(U_W)=W\) as subsets.  The two rational-domain structures agree by
the universal property of rational localization.  The finitely many
domains \(U_{W_\alpha}\) cover \(U\), because the \(W_\alpha\) cover \(V\)
and \(V\to U\) is bijective.  A finite cover by analytic domains is a
\(G\)-cover, so these are legitimate \(G\)-local charts on \(U\).

Write \(F=\mathcal O(U_W)\) and \(E=\mathcal O(W)\).  The hypothesis of the
proposition applied to \(U_W\) gives \(E^q\subseteq F\).  If
\(t\in E^\times\), then
\[
                         T=t^q\in F,
              \qquad S=(t^{-1})^q\in F.
\]
The map \(F\to E\) is injective: the restricted map
\(W\to U_W\) is surjective, so its kernel is nilpotent, while \(F\) is
reduced because \(U_W\) is an analytic domain in the reduced space \(X\).
Since \(TS=1\) in \(E\), it follows that \(TS=1\) in \(F\).  Thus \(T\) is
an analytic unit on \(U_W\), not merely a function with nonzero pointwise
values.

Apply this to every \(t_{\alpha j}\) in
\eqref{eq:p061-frobenius-upstairs-rpl}, writing
\(T_{\alpha j}=t_{\alpha j}^q\).  On \(W_\alpha\),
\[
 \sum_j\lambda_{\alpha j}\log|t_{\alpha j}|
 =f^*\!\left(
       \sum_j\frac{\lambda_{\alpha j}}q\log|T_{\alpha j}|
            \right).
\]
The left side is \(f^*g\).  Surjectivity
\(W_\alpha\to U_{W_\alpha}\) therefore yields
\[
       g|_{U_{W_\alpha}}
       =\sum_j\frac{\lambda_{\alpha j}}q
                         \log|T_{\alpha j}|.
\]
Real coefficients are divisible by \(q\).  These expressions on the
rational \(G\)-cover prove that \(g|_U\) is \(\mathbf R\)-PL.  Since strict
affinoid domains \(U\) form a \(G\)-cover of \(X\),
\cite[\S5.2(4)]{GJR26} finishes the proof.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}
\label{thm:p061-simplicial-toric-ph-rpl}
Let \(K\) be a complete non-Archimedean field with nontrivial absolute
value, let \(N\) be a lattice, and let
\(\sigma\subset N_{\mathbf R}\) be a strongly convex simplicial rational
polyhedral cone, not necessarily full dimensional.  Let
\(X_{\sigma,N}\) be the associated split affine toric \(K\)-variety, and
let \(U\) be a good strict analytic domain in
\(X_{\sigma,N}^{\mathrm{an}}\).  Then every classically pluriharmonic
function
\[
                              h:U\longrightarrow\mathbf R
\]
is \(\mathbf R\)-PL.  Moreover, \(h\) is harmonic in the sense of
Gubler--Jell--Rabinoff.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Put
\[
              N_\sigma=N\cap\operatorname{span}_{\mathbf R}(\sigma),
\]
and write \(r=\dim\sigma\).  The subgroup \(N_\sigma\) is saturated in
\(N\): if a nonzero integer multiple of an element of \(N\) lies in the
displayed real span, then the element itself lies in that span.  Thus
\(N/N_\sigma\) is free.  Choose a lattice complement \(N_{\mathrm c}\),
and let \(v_1,\ldots,v_r\) be the primitive ray generators of
\(\sigma\).  Simpliciality says that these vectors are linearly independent
and span \(N_{\sigma,\mathbf R}\).  Therefore
\[
        N'=\mathbf Z v_1\oplus\cdots\oplus\mathbf Z v_r
                      \oplus N_{\mathrm c}\subseteq N
\]
has finite index.  Relative to \(N'\), the cone is smooth, including when
\(r<\operatorname{rank}N\), and
\begin{equation}
 \label{eq:p061-simplicial-smooth-cover}
       X_{\sigma,N'}\simeq
       \mathbf A^r_K\times\mathbf G_{m,K}^{\operatorname{rank}N-r}.
\end{equation}

Let \(M=\operatorname{Hom}(N,\mathbf Z)\) and
\(M'=\operatorname{Hom}(N',\mathbf Z)\).  Then \(M\subseteq M'\) and
\(H=M'/M\) is finite.  Write
\[
 A_K=K[\sigma^\vee\cap M],
 \qquad B_K=K[\sigma^\vee\cap M'].
\]
The inclusion \(A_K\subseteq B_K\) is finite.  Indeed, for every
\(m'\in\sigma^\vee\cap M'\), some positive multiple \(d m'\) lies in
\(M\), and \(\chi^{m'}\) satisfies
\[
                         T^d-\chi^{d m'}=0
\]
over \(A_K\).  The algebra \(B_K\) is of finite type by Gordan's lemma, so
finite type plus integrality gives finiteness.  It is surjective on spectra
by lying over.  The \(H\)-grading of \(B_K\) has degree-zero subring exactly
\(A_K\), hence the finite toric morphism
\begin{equation}
 \label{eq:p061-simplicial-full-cover}
             X_{\sigma,N'}\longrightarrow X_{\sigma,N}
\end{equation}
is the quotient by the finite diagonalizable group \(D(H)\).  No flatness
claim is made or used.

We now split the quotient over a finite extension of \(K\).  If
\(\operatorname{char}K=0\), put \(M_1=M\) and let \(n\) be the exponent
of \(H\).  If \(\operatorname{char}K=p>0\), write canonically
\[
                              H=H_p\oplus H_{p'},
\]
and let \(M_1\subseteq M'\) be the inverse image of \(H_p\).  Then
\[
                       M_1/M=H_p,
             \qquad M'/M_1=H_{p'},
\]
and we let \(n\) be the exponent of \(H_{p'}\).  In either case, choose a
finite Galois extension \(L/K\) containing all \(n\)-th roots of unity;
take \(L=K\) if \(n=1\).  This extension exists because \(T^n-1\) is
separable: in characteristic zero this is automatic, and in characteristic
\(p\) the integer \(n\) is prime to \(p\).  Notice that this uses the
characteristic of \(K\), not its residue characteristic.  A finite extension
of the complete field \(K\) is complete.

Over \(L\), the factorization of \eqref{eq:p061-simplicial-full-cover} is
\begin{equation}
 \label{eq:p061-simplicial-factorization}
 X_{\sigma,N',L}\longrightarrow X_{\sigma,N_1,L}
                         \longrightarrow X_{\sigma,N,L},
\end{equation}
where \(N'\subseteq N_1\subseteq N\) is dual to
\(M\subseteq M_1\subseteq M'\).  The first arrow is the quotient by the
finite constant group obtained by splitting \(D(M'/M_1)\) over \(L\).
In characteristic zero the second arrow is the identity.

Suppose now that \(\operatorname{char}K=p>0\).  Choose
\(q=p^e\) annihilating \(H_p\).  Then \(qM_1\subseteq M\).  If
\[
 A=L[\sigma^\vee\cap M],
 \qquad B=L[\sigma^\vee\cap M_1],
\]
then \(B^q\subseteq A\): for
\(b=\sum_m c_m\chi^m\), Frobenius gives
\[
                         b^q=\sum_m c_m^q\chi^{qm}\in A.
\]
The finite map \(\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A\) is
radicial.  Indeed, if two primes of \(B\) lie above the same prime of
\(A\), then \(b\) in the first prime implies \(b^q\) lies in the base prime
and hence \(b\) lies in the second; symmetry gives equality.  The same
\(q\)-power calculation makes every residue-field extension purely
inseparable.  Finiteness and lying over give surjectivity.

We also record the analytic base-change property needed to apply
\Cref{prop:p061-frobenius-rpl-descent}.  Let \(Z=\mathcal M(C)\) be any
strict affinoid domain in \(X_{\sigma,N,L}^{\mathrm{an}}\), and let
\(Z_1=\mathcal M(D)\) be its inverse image under the second arrow of
\eqref{eq:p061-simplicial-factorization}.  Compatibility of finite
analytification with affinoid base change
\cite[Fact~4.1.16 and Definition~4.2.5]{Temkin2015Berkovich} gives
\begin{equation}
 \label{eq:p061-simplicial-affinoid-base-change}
                              D=C\otimes_A B.
\end{equation}
The ordinary tensor product is already complete: \(B\) is a finite
\(A\)-module, so the right side is a finite \(C\)-module, and a finite
presentation realizes it as a quotient of a finite free \(C\)-module by a
closed submodule.  Every \(z\in D\) is a finite sum
\(z=\sum_i c_i\otimes b_i\), whence
\[
                     z^q=\sum_i c_i^q\otimes b_i^q\in C.
\]
Thus \(D^q\subseteq C\) on every required affinoid domain, and the same
calculation applies after every rational localization.  The algebra \(C\)
is reduced because the split toric variety is geometrically integral and
\(Z\) is an analytic domain.  Surjectivity of the finite radicial map then
makes \(C\to D\) injective.  All hypotheses of
\Cref{prop:p061-frobenius-rpl-descent} are satisfied.

Let \(h:U\to\mathbf R\) be classically pluriharmonic.  By
\cite[Proposition~7.2(6),(7)]{GR25Classical}, its scalar pullback \(h_L\)
to \(U_L\) is classically pluriharmonic.  It is enough to prove that \(h_L\)
is \(\mathbf R\)-PL on every strict affinoid domain \(Z\) in \(U_L\).  Let
\(Z_1\) be the inverse image of \(Z\) under the second arrow of
\eqref{eq:p061-simplicial-factorization}, and let \(V\) be the inverse image
of \(Z_1\) under the first arrow.  Both are strict affinoid because the
arrows are finite.  The space \(V\) is an analytic domain in the smooth
space in \eqref{eq:p061-simplicial-smooth-cover}, hence it is good, strict,
and quasi-smooth.  The same cited proposition shows that the pullback of
\(h_L\) to \(V\) remains classically pluriharmonic.
\Cref{thm:p061-quasismooth-ph-rpl} makes that pullback \(\mathbf R\)-PL.

The target \(Z_1\) is the analytic categorical quotient of \(V\) by the
finite constant group \(G=D(M'/M_1)_L\).  For completeness, this remains
true after restriction to \(Z_1\): if \(C_1=\mathcal O(Z_1)\) and
\(E=\mathcal O(V)\), then the Reynolds idempotent
\[
                         \frac1{|G|}\sum_{\gamma\in G}\gamma
\]
is a bounded projector on \(E\) with image \(E^G=C_1\).  Here
\(|G|\neq0\) in \(L\); it need not be a unit in the valuation ring.  The
projector commutes with the finite affinoid base change.
\Cref{prop:p061-finite-group-rpl-descent-candidate} therefore descends
\(\mathbf R\)-PL regularity from \(V\) to \(Z_1\).

In characteristic \(p>0\),
\Cref{prop:p061-frobenius-rpl-descent} and
\eqref{eq:p061-simplicial-affinoid-base-change} descend it further from
\(Z_1\) to \(Z\).  In characteristic zero the second arrow is the identity.
Thus \(h_L\) is \(\mathbf R\)-PL on a \(G\)-cover of \(U_L\), and hence on
\(U_L\) by \cite[\S5.2(4)]{GJR26}.
\cite[Corollary~5.12]{GJR26} now descends
\(\mathbf R\)-piecewise linearity from \(L\) to \(K\), giving that \(h\) is
\(\mathbf R\)-PL on \(U\).

Finally, \(h\) and \(-h\) are classically psh by the definition of
classical pluriharmonicity.  By \cite[Theorem~4.3]{GR25Classical}, classical
psh and semipositivity agree for \(\mathbf R\)-PL functions.  Both signs of
\(h\) are therefore semipositive, which is precisely
Gubler--Jell--Rabinoff harmonicity by \cite[Definition~7.2]{GJR26}.
\end{proof}
